target: AArch64 native ZealC on PCI QEMU

checks.evidence: The installed Wallpaper Desktop Palette icon launched the editor. The random-color key changed palette entry 0 and scanout. The # hex-entry path accepted 123456; the live entry's R/G/B channels were 18/52/86 and scanout changed. Escape closed the editor, retained the edited value, and the terminal recovered with 40+2=42.

The combined test also passed the installed desktop, all six controls, focused Home and Terminal shells, Stats toggle, NetLog open/write/close/reopen, and Telnet form, local fixture connection, typed input, socket close, and task exit.

scope_note: Automated disposable-disk QEMU acceptance only. It covers Palette Editor random-color and hex-entry workflows. Arrow-key selection, successful save persistence, opening a saved palette, arbitrary HomeSys customization, and live UTM/Pi desktop behavior remain unverified. Save As cancellation failed in the follow-up below. The application remains partial in the source ledger because its full workflow and host-specific live coverage are not complete.

save_as_follow_up.steps: From the installed Wallpaper Desktop, open Palette Editor, change a color, enter Ctrl+A, then press Escape in the filename form.
save_as_follow_up.observed: The FileName form renders. Escape reaches an unresolved external call in PESave (one baseline run reported PESave+0xd8); the serial session then reports that it is unavailable. No palette file was verified as saved, and Save As remains unaccepted.
save_as_follow_up.target: AArch64 native ZealC on PCI QEMU, disposable disk
save_as_follow_up.source_change: None; upstream/pinned source and runtime were not changed by the follow-up probe.
